subproblem.title: Injective area formula on an open Lipschitz domain, in integral form
subproblem.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, B ⊆ ℝⁿ open, ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ K-Lipschitz on B (K ∈ ℝ≥0) and injective on B, and g : ℝᴺ → ℝ continuous. Then ∫_{ψ(B)} g dHⁿ = ∫_B g(ψ(v))·Jψ(v) dLⁿ(v), where Jψ(v) := normDet(Dψ(v)) with Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v, Hⁿ = μHE[n] and Lⁿ = volume; both sides are Bochner integrals (no integrability assumption).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (B : Set (Rn n)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N) (K : ℝ≥0), IsOpen B → LipschitzOnWith K ψ B → InjOn ψ B → ∀ g : Rn N → ℝ, Continuous g → ∫ y in ψ '' B, g y ∂μHE[n] = ∫ v in B, g (ψ v) * (fderiv ℝ ψ v).toLinearMap.normDet
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Selected-node proof step 4 (with step 3(a) for measurability of the Jacobian): Simon Ch. 2, (3.2) and (3.5), the area formula for a one-to-one Lipschitz map on a measurable domain, put in integral form. No sibling child is used. Import note: the SimonGMT area formula on a Lipschitz domain lives in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaDomain, which GMT.Ch03.Submission does not import; the formalization adds `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaDomain` (prebuilt pinned package; the frozen statement elaborates identically with it).

Notation. Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ; Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝᴺ; Γ := ψ(B); Dψ(v) := fderiv ℝ ψ v; Jψ(v) := normDet(Dψ(v)).

1. Jacobian. Jψ(v) ≥ 0 for all v (LinearMap.normDet_nonneg). Jψ is Borel measurable on ℝⁿ: v ↦ Dψ(v) is measurable for every map ψ (Mathlib measurable_fderiv), and A ↦ normDet(A) is continuous on ℝⁿ →L ℝᴺ, hence measurable; compose. (Continuity of normDet is SimonGMT Chapter02.continuous_normDet, visible after the AreaDomain import. Its proof: normDet(A) ≥ 0 and normDet(A)² = det(A* ∘L A) (ContinuousLinearMap.normDet_sq), so normDet(A) = √det(A* ∘L A). That is a composition of the continuous maps A ↦ A* (a linear isometric equivalence), A ↦ A* ∘L A (Continuous.clm_comp), det (ContinuousLinearMap.continuous_det) and √.) Put j(v) := Jψ(v).toNNReal ∈ ℝ≥0. Then j is measurable (Measurable.real_toNNReal), (j(v) : ℝ) = Jψ(v) (Real.coe_toNNReal, as Jψ ≥ 0), and (j(v) : [0, ∞]) = ofReal(Jψ(v)) (definition of ENNReal.ofReal).

2. Measurability facts. B is open, hence Borel. ψ is continuous on B (LipschitzOnWith.continuousOn), hence a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞B (ContinuousOn.aemeasurable). Let ν := (Lⁿ⌞B).withDensity(j), i.e. the measure with density v ↦ (j(v) : [0, ∞]) with respect to Lⁿ⌞B. Since ν ≪ Lⁿ⌞B (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous), ψ is also a.e.-measurable for ν (AEMeasurable.mono_ac). Finally Γ = ψ(B) is Borel by the Lusin-Souslin theorem (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn: B is Borel in the Polish space ℝⁿ and ψ is continuous and injective on B).

3. Reduction of the measure identity. Claim: Hⁿ⌞Γ = ψ_#ν as measures on ℝᴺ. By extensionality (Measure.ext) it suffices to fix a Borel set E ⊆ ℝᴺ and to show Hⁿ(E ∩ Γ) = ν(ψ⁻¹(E)): indeed (Hⁿ⌞Γ)(E) = Hⁿ(E ∩ Γ) (Measure.restrict_apply, E measurable), (ψ_#ν)(E) = ν(ψ⁻¹(E)) (Measure.map_apply_of_aemeasurable), and ν(ψ⁻¹(E)) = ∫⁻_{ψ⁻¹(E)} j d(Lⁿ⌞B) (withDensity_apply', valid for every set because Lⁿ⌞B is s-finite).

4. Weighted area formula. Let w(v) := 1_E(ψ(v)) ∈ {0, 1} ⊆ [0, ∞]; w is a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞B (the measurable indicator of the Borel set E composed with the a.e.-measurable ψ). Apply SimonGMT Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum (Simon (3.5)) with s = B (open, hence null-measurable), the K-Lipschitz map ψ on B, and the weight w. After rewriting finrank ℝⁿ = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin) it reads
   ∫⁻_{ℝᴺ} weightedAreaFiberSum B ψ w y dHⁿ(y) = ∫⁻_B ofReal(areaJacobianWithin ψ B v)·w(v) dLⁿ(v),
where weightedAreaFiberSum B ψ w y is the sum Σ' of w(v) over the fibre {v : v ∈ B ∧ ψ(v) = y} (SimonGMT areaFiber), and areaJacobianWithin ψ B v = normDet(fderivWithin ℝ ψ B v).

5. Left side. Fix y ∈ ℝᴺ. If y ∉ Γ, the fibre is empty and the sum is 0 = 1_{E∩Γ}(y) (tsum_empty). If y = ψ(v₀) with v₀ ∈ B, then any two fibre elements a, b satisfy ψ(a) = y = ψ(b) with a, b ∈ B, so a = b by injectivity of ψ on B; the fibre is therefore a subsingleton containing v₀ and the sum equals w(v₀) = 1_E(ψ(v₀)) = 1_E(y) = 1_{E∩Γ}(y) (tsum_eq_single). Hence the integrand on the left is the indicator 1_{E∩Γ}, and since E ∩ Γ is Borel (step 2) the left side equals Hⁿ(E ∩ Γ) (lintegral_indicator_one).

6. Right side. For v ∈ B, openness of B gives fderivWithin ℝ ψ B v = fderiv ℝ ψ v (fderivWithin_of_isOpen), so areaJacobianWithin ψ B v = Jψ(v) and ofReal(areaJacobianWithin ψ B v)·w(v) = ofReal(Jψ(v))·1_E(ψ(v)) = 1_{ψ⁻¹(E)}(v)·j(v) (check the cases ψ(v) ∈ E and ψ(v) ∉ E). Hence (setLIntegral_congr_fun on the Borel set B) the right side equals ∫⁻ 1_{ψ⁻¹(E)}·j d(Lⁿ⌞B) = ∫⁻_{ψ⁻¹(E)} j d(Lⁿ⌞B) (lintegral_indicator₀; ψ⁻¹(E) is null-measurable for Lⁿ⌞B because ψ is a.e.-measurable there, AEMeasurable.nullMeasurable), which is ν(ψ⁻¹(E)) by step 3.

7. Steps 4-6 give Hⁿ(E ∩ Γ) = ν(ψ⁻¹(E)) for every Borel set E ⊆ ℝᴺ, so by step 3, Hⁿ⌞Γ = ψ_#ν.

8. Integral identity. By step 7,
   ∫_Γ g dHⁿ = ∫ g d(ψ_#ν) = ∫ g(ψ(v)) dν(v) = ∫ j(v)•g(ψ(v)) d(Lⁿ⌞B)(v) = ∫_B g(ψ(v))·Jψ(v) dv.
The second equality is the change of variables for push-forward measures (integral_map: ψ is a.e.-measurable for ν, and g is continuous, hence a.e.-strongly measurable for ψ_#ν); the third is integration against a density (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul, j measurable); the fourth uses NNReal.smul_def and (j(v) : ℝ) = Jψ(v). Each of these is an identity of Bochner integrals valid without any integrability assumption (integrability is transported along the same identities, and both sides are 0 in the non-integrable case), so continuity of g is the only hypothesis needed. ∎

subproblem.title: Derivative bounds for a C¹ map that is Lipschitz and has a lower Lipschitz bound on an open set
subproblem.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, B ⊆ ℝⁿ open, ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ of class C¹ on B and K-Lipschitz on B (K ∈ ℝ≥0), and c ∈ ℝ with c|u − u'| ≤ |ψ(u) − ψ(u')| for all u, u' ∈ B. Then for every v ∈ B the derivative Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v satisfies ‖Dψ(v)‖ ≤ K (operator norm) and c|w| ≤ |Dψ(v) w| for every w ∈ ℝⁿ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (B : Set (Rn n)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N) (K : ℝ≥0) (c : ℝ), IsOpen B → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ B → LipschitzOnWith K ψ B → (∀ u ∈ B, ∀ u' ∈ B, c * ‖u - u'‖ ≤ ‖ψ u - ψ u'‖) → ∀ v ∈ B, ‖fderiv ℝ ψ v‖ ≤ K ∧ ∀ w : Rn n, c * ‖w‖ ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ ψ v w‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Selected-node proof (root.chart_tangent_differential-a1.chart_blowup_tangent-a1), steps 1 and 2: the derivative of a map that is Lipschitz, resp. satisfies a lower Lipschitz bound, on an open set (the facts about the C¹ charts used in Simon's proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒', chapter-03.txt lines 113-143, and Remark 1.5(2)). No sign assumption on c is needed.

Notation. ℝⁿ = Rn n with the Euclidean norm; Dψ(v) := fderiv ℝ ψ v : ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝᴺ with its operator norm ‖·‖.

1. Differentiability. Fix v ∈ B and put D := Dψ(v). Since B is open and v ∈ B, B is a neighbourhood of v (IsOpen.mem_nhds). Since ψ is C¹ on B, it is differentiable on B (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn, as 1 ≠ 0), hence differentiable at v because B ∈ 𝓝 v (DifferentiableOn.differentiableAt); so ψ has Fréchet derivative D at v (DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt).

2. Upper bound. ψ is K-Lipschitz on the neighbourhood B of v, hence ‖D‖ ≤ K (Mathlib norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitzOn with s = B ∈ 𝓝 v). (Underlying argument: for w ∈ ℝⁿ and small t > 0, v + t w ∈ B and |ψ(v + t w) − ψ(v)| ≤ K t |w|; dividing by t and letting t ↓ 0 gives |D w| ≤ K |w| for every w, i.e. ‖D‖ ≤ K.)

3. Lower bound, admissible t. Fix w ∈ ℝⁿ. The map t ↦ v + t•w is continuous with value v at t = 0, so v + t•w → v as t → 0⁺ (filter 𝓝[>]0); since B ∈ 𝓝 v, eventually in 𝓝[>]0 we have v + t•w ∈ B, and also t > 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin).

4. For every such t (t > 0 and v + t•w ∈ B), the hypothesis applied to u = v + t•w and u' = v gives c·|t•w| ≤ |ψ(v + t•w) − ψ(v)|, i.e. c·t·|w| ≤ |ψ(v + t•w) − ψ(v)|. Multiplying by t⁻¹ > 0: c|w| = t⁻¹·(c·(t·|w|)) ≤ t⁻¹·|ψ(v + t•w) − ψ(v)| = |t⁻¹•(ψ(v + t•w) − ψ(v))|.

5. Limit of the difference quotients. As t → 0⁺ we have |t⁻¹| = t⁻¹ → +∞ (tendsto_inv_nhdsGT_zero). Hence the derivative of ψ at v (HasFDerivAt.lim, applied with direction w and the scalars c(t) = t⁻¹, for which (c(t))⁻¹ = t) gives t⁻¹•(ψ(v + t•w) − ψ(v)) → D w as t → 0⁺, and by continuity of the norm |t⁻¹•(ψ(v + t•w) − ψ(v))| → |D w|.

6. Conclusion. By step 4 the quantities converging in step 5 are eventually ≥ c|w|, so the limit satisfies c|w| ≤ |D w| (ge_of_tendsto). Since v ∈ B and w ∈ ℝⁿ were arbitrary, steps 2 and 6 give ‖Dψ(v)‖ ≤ K and c|w| ≤ |Dψ(v) w| for all v ∈ B and w ∈ ℝⁿ. ∎

theorem Submission.chartTD_chart_fderiv_bounds : (∀ (n N : ℕ) (B : Set (Rn n)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N) (K : ℝ≥0) (c : ℝ), IsOpen B → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ B → LipschitzOnWith K ψ B → (∀ u ∈ B, ∀ u' ∈ B, c * ‖u - u'‖ ≤ ‖ψ u - ψ u'‖) → ∀ v ∈ B, ‖fderiv ℝ ψ v‖ ≤ K ∧ ∀ w : Rn n, c * ‖w‖ ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ ψ v w‖) := by
  intro n N B ψ K c hB hψ hLip hlow v hv
  have hBv : B ∈ 𝓝 v := hB.mem_nhds hv
  refine ⟨norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitzOn ℝ hBv hLip, fun w => ?_⟩
  have hd : HasFDerivAt ψ (fderiv ℝ ψ v) v :=
    ((hψ.differentiableOn one_ne_zero).differentiableAt hBv).hasFDerivAt
  have hlim := hd.lim w (c := fun t : ℝ => t⁻¹) (l := 𝓝[>] (0:ℝ)) (by
    refine (tendsto_inv_nhdsGT_zero (𝕜 := ℝ)).congr' ?_
    filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with t ht
    simp [abs_of_pos (show (0:ℝ) < t from ht)])
  have hnorm := (continuous_norm.tendsto _).comp hlim
  refine ge_of_tendsto hnorm ?_
  have hev : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0:ℝ), v + t • w ∈ B := by
    have : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => v + t • w) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 v) := by
      have : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => v + t • w) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 (v + (0:ℝ) • w)) :=
        ((continuous_const.add (continuous_id.smul continuous_const)).tendsto 0)
      simpa using this.mono_left nhdsWithin_le_nhds
    exact this hBv
  filter_upwards [hev, self_mem_nhdsWithin] with t ht htpos
  simp only [Function.comp, inv_inv]
  have h1 := hlow (v + t • w) ht v hv
  rw [add_sub_cancel_left, norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg (le_of_lt htpos)] at h1
  rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg (inv_nonneg.mpr (le_of_lt htpos))]
  have htpos' : (0:ℝ) < t := htpos
  calc c * ‖w‖ = t⁻¹ * (c * (t * ‖w‖)) := by field_simp
    _ ≤ t⁻¹ * ‖ψ (v + t • w) - ψ v‖ := by gcongr

end GMT.Ch03

subproblem.title: Hadamard-type bound normDet(A) ≤ ‖A‖ⁿ for linear maps ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ
subproblem.statement: For all n, N ∈ ℕ and every continuous linear map A : ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝᴺ, normDet(A) ≤ ‖A‖ⁿ, where ‖A‖ is the operator norm and normDet(A) = √det(A*A) (Mathlib LinearMap.normDet of A.toLinearMap).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn N), A.toLinearMap.normDet ≤ ‖A‖ ^ n
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Selected-node proof step 3(b): the bound on the area Jacobian used for domination, obtained from the linear area formula (Simon Ch. 2, (3.1)) and the Lipschitz image estimate for Hausdorff measure.

Notation. Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ; Hᵐ := μHE[m] (Euclidean Hausdorff measure); S := B̄₁(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ (closed unit ball); m := finrank ℝ ℝⁿ, so m = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin); ‖A‖ is the operator norm and ‖A‖₊ its ℝ≥0-valued version.

1. Linear area formula (Simon (3.1); Mathlib LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume applied to A as a linear map and the set S): Hᵐ(A(S)) = ofReal(normDet A)·Lⁿ(S) in [0, ∞].

2. Lipschitz estimate. A is ‖A‖₊-Lipschitz on ℝⁿ (ContinuousLinearMap.lipschitzWith), in particular on S, so the Hausdorff-measure image estimate (SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn with exponent m) gives Hᵐ(A(S)) ≤ ‖A‖₊ᵐ·Hᵐ(S). Since m = finrank ℝⁿ, Hᵐ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so Hᵐ(A(S)) ≤ ‖A‖₊ᵐ·Lⁿ(S).

3. Cancellation. Steps 1 and 2 give ofReal(normDet A)·Lⁿ(S) ≤ ‖A‖₊ᵐ·Lⁿ(S). The closed unit ball satisfies 0 < Lⁿ(S) (Metric.measure_closedBall_pos, radius 1 > 0) and Lⁿ(S) < ∞ (measure_closedBall_lt_top), so the factor Lⁿ(S) cancels (ENNReal.mul_le_mul_iff_left): ofReal(normDet A) ≤ ‖A‖₊ᵐ = ‖A‖₊ⁿ.

4. Back to ℝ. The coercion of ‖A‖₊ to [0, ∞] is ofReal ‖A‖, and ofReal(‖A‖)ⁿ = ofReal(‖A‖ⁿ) (ENNReal.ofReal_pow, ‖A‖ ≥ 0). Hence ofReal(normDet A) ≤ ofReal(‖A‖ⁿ), and since ‖A‖ⁿ ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff yields normDet(A) ≤ ‖A‖ⁿ. (For n = 0 the same argument applies verbatim: ℝ⁰ = {0} = S, L⁰(S) = 1, and both sides equal 1.) ∎

theorem Submission.chartTD_normDet_le_opNorm_pow : (∀ (n N : ℕ) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn N), A.toLinearMap.normDet ≤ ‖A‖ ^ n) := by
  intro n N A
  have hfin : finrank ℝ (Rn n) = n := finrank_euclideanSpace_fin
  set S : Set (Rn n) := Metric.closedBall 0 1 with hS
  have h1 := LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume A.toLinearMap S
  have h2 := Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn
    (finrank ℝ (Rn n)) (A.lipschitzWith.lipschitzOnWith (s := S))
  rw [InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume] at h2
  have hcoe : (A.toLinearMap : Rn n → Rn N) '' S = A '' S := rfl
  rw [← hcoe, h1] at h2
  have hpos : 0 < volume S := Metric.measure_closedBall_pos _ _ one_pos
  have hfinite : volume S < ∞ := measure_closedBall_lt_top
  have h3 : ENNReal.ofReal A.toLinearMap.normDet ≤ (‖A‖₊ : ℝ≥0∞) ^ finrank ℝ (Rn n) :=
    (ENNReal.mul_le_mul_iff_left hpos.ne' hfinite.ne).mp h2
  rw [hfin] at h3
  have h4 : ENNReal.ofReal A.toLinearMap.normDet ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (‖A‖ ^ n) := by
    rw [ENNReal.ofReal_pow (norm_nonneg _)]
    simpa [ofReal_norm, enorm_eq_nnnorm] using h3
  exact (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff (by positivity)).mp h4

subproblem.title: Blow-up limit of the pulled-back chart integral (substitution and dominated convergence)
subproblem.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, B ⊆ ℝⁿ open, ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ of class C¹ on B and K-Lipschitz on B (K ∈ ℝ≥0), and c > 0 with c|u − u'| ≤ |ψ(u) − ψ(u')| for all u, u' ∈ B. Let u ∈ B and f ∈ C_c(ℝᴺ, ℝ). Writing Jψ(v) := normDet(Dψ(v)) (Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v) and η_{x,r}(z) := r⁻¹(z − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap), we have r⁻ⁿ ∫_B f(η_{ψ(u),r}(ψ(v)))·Jψ(v) dv → Jψ(u)·∫_{ℝⁿ} f(Dψ(u) y) dy as r → 0⁺ (Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ; Bochner integrals).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (B : Set (Rn n)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N) (K : ℝ≥0) (c : ℝ), IsOpen B → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ B → LipschitzOnWith K ψ B → 0 < c → (∀ u ∈ B, ∀ u' ∈ B, c * ‖u - u'‖ ≤ ‖ψ u - ψ u'‖) → ∀ u ∈ B, ∀ f : C_c(Rn N, ℝ), Tendsto (fun r : ℝ ↦ (r ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ v in B, f (blowUpMap (ψ u) r (ψ v)) * (fderiv ℝ ψ v).toLinearMap.normDet) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 ((fderiv ℝ ψ u).toLinearMap.normDet * ∫ y, f (fderiv ℝ ψ u y)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Selected-node proof steps 5-9 (with the facts of steps 1 and 3): the blow-up of the pulled-back chart integral and dominated convergence (Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' and Remark 1.5(2), chapter-03.txt lines 87-90 and 113-143, for a single bi-Lipschitz C¹ chart). Uses the siblings fderiv_bounds (Submission.chartTD_chart_fderiv_bounds) and normdet_le_opnorm_pow (Submission.chartTD_normDet_le_opNorm_pow). No extra import is needed.

Notation. Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ; Dψ(v) := fderiv ℝ ψ v; L := Dψ(u); Jψ(v) := normDet(Dψ(v)); J := Jψ(u); for r > 0, η_r(z) := blowUpMap (ψ u) r z = r⁻¹•(z − ψ(u)).

1. Facts about ψ and Jψ. (a) Jψ ≥ 0 (LinearMap.normDet_nonneg). (b) The map A ↦ normDet(A) on ℝⁿ →L ℝᴺ is continuous. Indeed normDet(A) ≥ 0 and normDet(A)² = det(A* ∘L A) (ContinuousLinearMap.normDet_sq; over ℝ the scalar cast is the identity), so normDet(A) = √det(A* ∘L A) (Real.sqrt_sq). That is a composition of continuous maps: A ↦ A* (the adjoint is a linear isometric equivalence), A ↦ A* ∘L A (Continuous.clm_comp), det on ℝⁿ →L ℝⁿ (ContinuousLinearMap.continuous_det) and √ (Real.continuous_sqrt). (This is also SimonGMT Chapter02.continuous_normDet, visible after `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaDomain`.) Since v ↦ Dψ(v) is measurable (measurable_fderiv), Jψ = normDet ∘ Dψ is Borel on ℝⁿ. (c) For v ∈ B, Jψ(v) ≤ ‖Dψ(v)‖ⁿ ≤ Kⁿ, by the sibling normdet_le_opnorm_pow and the bound ‖Dψ(v)‖ ≤ K from the sibling fderiv_bounds (pow_le_pow_left₀, norms being ≥ 0). (d) Jψ is continuous at u: v ↦ Dψ(v) is continuous on the open set B (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen with 1 ≤ 1), hence continuous at u ∈ B, and normDet is continuous by 1(b). (e) ψ is continuous on B (Lipschitz on B), and ψ has Fréchet derivative L at u (ψ is C¹ on the open set B ∋ u, so ContDiffOn.differentiableOn and DifferentiableOn.differentiableAt apply).

2. Constants from f. f is continuous with compact support. Choose M with |f(z)| ≤ M for all z ∈ ℝᴺ (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous); then M ≥ |f(0)| ≥ 0. The compact set tsupport f is bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ B̄_R(0) for some R (IsCompact.isBounded, Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall); hence f(z) ≠ 0 implies |z| ≤ R (subset_tsupport).

3. Substitution. Fix r > 0 and define h_r(v) := f(η_r(ψ(v)))·Jψ(v) and G_r(y) := (1_B·h_r)(u + r•y), where 1_B·h_r denotes the indicator B.indicator h_r. Since B is Borel, ∫_B h_r = ∫_{ℝⁿ} 1_B·h_r (integral_indicator). By the scaling formula for Haar measure (Measure.integral_comp_smul, applied to y ↦ (1_B·h_r)(u + y) and the scalar r), ∫ (1_B·h_r)(u + r•y) dy = |(r^{finrank ℝⁿ})⁻¹|·∫ (1_B·h_r)(u + y) dy, and by translation invariance (integral_add_left_eq_self) ∫ (1_B·h_r)(u + y) dy = ∫ (1_B·h_r)(y) dy. Since finrank ℝⁿ = n and r > 0, |(rⁿ)⁻¹| = (rⁿ)⁻¹. Hence, for every r > 0,
   (rⁿ)⁻¹·∫_B f(η_r(ψ(v)))·Jψ(v) dv = ∫_{ℝⁿ} G_r(y) dy.
(These are identities of Bochner integrals valid without integrability assumptions.)

4. Measurability of G_r (r > 0). Let S_r := {y : u + r•y ∈ B}, the preimage of the open set B under the continuous map y ↦ u + r•y; S_r is open. By the definition of the indicator, G_r = 1_{S_r}·(y ↦ h_r(u + r•y)). On S_r, y ↦ f(η_r(ψ(u + r•y))) is continuous (f and η_r are continuous, ψ is continuous on B, and u + r•y ∈ B for y ∈ S_r), hence a.e.-strongly measurable for Lⁿ⌞S_r (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable); y ↦ Jψ(u + r•y) is Borel by 1(b). Their product is a.e.-strongly measurable for Lⁿ⌞S_r, and therefore G_r is a.e.-strongly measurable for Lⁿ (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff, S_r Borel).

5. Domination. Let β(y) := M·Kⁿ·1_{B̄_{R/c}(0)}(y) ≥ 0. β is Lⁿ-integrable: it is a constant on the closed ball B̄_{R/c}(0), which has finite measure (integrableOn_const with measure_closedBall_lt_top, then IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator). Claim: |G_r(y)| ≤ β(y) for every r > 0 and every y. If u + r•y ∉ B, then G_r(y) = 0 ≤ β(y). If u + r•y ∈ B and f(η_r(ψ(u + r•y))) = 0, then again G_r(y) = 0. Otherwise u + r•y ∈ B and f(η_r(ψ(u + r•y))) ≠ 0, so by step 2, |η_r(ψ(u + r•y))| = r⁻¹·|ψ(u + r•y) − ψ(u)| ≤ R, i.e. |ψ(u + r•y) − ψ(u)| ≤ r·R. The lower bound applied to u + r•y, u ∈ B gives c·r·|y| = c·|(u + r•y) − u| ≤ |ψ(u + r•y) − ψ(u)| ≤ r·R; dividing by r·c > 0 yields |y| ≤ R/c, i.e. y ∈ B̄_{R/c}(0), so β(y) = M·Kⁿ. In this case |G_r(y)| = |f(η_r(ψ(u + r•y)))|·Jψ(u + r•y) ≤ M·Kⁿ = β(y), by step 2 and 1(a), 1(c).

6. Pointwise limit. Fix y ∈ ℝⁿ and let r → 0⁺ (filter 𝓝[>]0). (i) u + r•y → u, and B ∈ 𝓝 u, so eventually u + r•y ∈ B and then G_r(y) = f(η_r(ψ(u + r•y)))·Jψ(u + r•y). (ii) η_r(ψ(u + r•y)) = r⁻¹•(ψ(u + r•y) − ψ(u)) → L y: apply HasFDerivAt.lim to the derivative L of ψ at u (1(e)) with direction y and scalars c(r) = r⁻¹, using |r⁻¹| = r⁻¹ → +∞ as r → 0⁺ (tendsto_inv_nhdsGT_zero) and (c(r))⁻¹ = r. (For y = 0 both sides are 0.) (iii) By continuity of f, f(η_r(ψ(u + r•y))) → f(L y). (iv) By 1(d) and (i), Jψ(u + r•y) → Jψ(u) = J. Hence G_r(y) → f(L y)·J (the limit of the product, transferred to G_r by the eventual equality in (i)).

7. Dominated convergence. The filter 𝓝[>]0 is countably generated. By steps 4, 5 and 6 (measurability and domination for all r > 0, i.e. eventually in 𝓝[>]0; pointwise convergence for every y), tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence gives ∫ G_r(y) dy → ∫ f(L y)·J dy as r → 0⁺. Moreover ∫ f(L y)·J dy = (∫ f(L y) dy)·J = J·∫ f(L y) dy (integral_mul_const, valid without integrability assumptions).

8. Conclusion. By step 3, the function r ↦ (rⁿ)⁻¹·∫_B f(η_r(ψ(v)))·Jψ(v) dv agrees with r ↦ ∫ G_r for every r > 0, i.e. on a set belonging to 𝓝[>]0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). Since eventually equal functions have the same limits (Tendsto.congr'), step 7 yields (rⁿ)⁻¹·∫_B f(η_r(ψ(v)))·Jψ(v) dv → Jψ(u)·∫_{ℝⁿ} f(Dψ(u) y) dy as r → 0⁺. (The case n = 0 needs no separate treatment.) ∎
